rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh means Moses is now among those who deny his benefactor, namely Pharaoh, for raising him.
rows.anchor: وأنت الآن من الكافرين لنعمتي أي لتربيتي إياك

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah's reading has Moses say he did the deed then while among the ignorant.
rows.anchor: قراءة عبد الله (قال فعلتها إذا وأنا من الجاهلين)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dāllīn and al-jāhilīn are synonymous: Arabic speakers say they lost or went astray from a road.
rows.anchor: الضالين والجاهلين يكونان بمعنى واحد لأنك تقول: جهلت الطريق

words: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses concedes that being raised was a favor, while stressing Pharaoh did not enslave him as he enslaved the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: نعمة إذ ربيتني ولم تستعبدني كاستعبادك بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits “and you left me alone”; that omitted contrast is clear from the example of sparing one servant while beating another.
rows.anchor: ثم يحذف (وتركتنى) والمعنى قائم معروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause with an may be nominative as an apposition explaining the favor, or accusative as the favor Moses is reproached for.
rows.anchor: أما الرفع فعلى قولك وتلك نعمة تمنها علي: تعبيدك بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs use both ʿabada and aʿbada for enslaving; an unnamed Arab's poem uses yaʿbudunī in this sense.
rows.anchor: أنشدني بعض العرب: علام يعبدني قومي وقد كثرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's question means “Will you listen to Moses?”; Moses, the intended respondent, supplies the answer rather than Pharaoh answering himself.
rows.anchor: إنما أراد بقوله: (ألا تستمعون) إلى قول موسى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he calls them to worship their Lord and their forefathers' Lord, then identifies this as the Lord of east, west, and everything between.
rows.anchor: أدعوكم إلى عبادته (ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Open an is the natural syntax because the clause is past and has a conditional force; kasra with a jussive reading is also correct.
rows.anchor: وجه الكلام أن تفتح (أن) لأنها ماضية وهي في مذهب جزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The first believers” means the first believers of their own era.
rows.anchor: (كنا أول المؤمنين) يقولون: أول مؤمني أهل زماننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirdhimma means a small band or company; qalīlūn and kathīrūn are valid Arabic plurals.
rows.anchor: يقول عصبة قليلة وقليلون وكثيرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic more often says a people are few or many with a singular adjective, since the quality applies collectively, but the plural is also grammatical.
rows.anchor: وأكثر كلام العرب أن يقولوا: قومك قليل وقومنا كثير

words: إلا من ظلم ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of the exception preserves the messengers' protection and safety in the afterlife; those mixing good and evil deeds instead fear and hope.
rows.anchor: إن الرسل معصومة مغفور لها آمنة يوم القيامة

words: إلا من ظلم ثم بدل حسنا بعد سوء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the unspoken group is everyone besides the messengers; a former polytheist who repents and does good is forgiven and no longer fears.
rows.anchor: لأن المعنى: لا يخاف المرسلون إنما الخوف على غيرهم

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat illā as equivalent to wa: the messengers and those who sinned then repented both do not fear.
rows.anchor: وقد قال بعض النحويين: إن (إلا) في اللغة بمنزلة الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ rejects making illā a conjunction: ordinary exception removes the following noun from the preceding group, as in “the people stood except ʿAbd Allāh.”
rows.anchor: لأني لا أجيز قام الناس إلا عبد الله، وهو قائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A usage like “one thousand besides another thousand” could take illā in place of siwā; that is a semantic parallel to conjunction, not illā itself being wa.
rows.anchor: عليك ألف سوى ألف آخر، فإن وضعت (إلا) في هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: On Ubayy's reading, the an in the basmala is connected to the following an lā taʿlū, so the message means “I have been sent that you not be arrogant.”
rows.anchor: هي (أن) التي في قوله (أن لا تعلوا على)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated an can express one underlying clause, as in 23:35, which asks whether they are promised resurrection after becoming dust and bones.
rows.anchor: فأنكم مكررة ومعناها واحد والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen calls for consultation “a fatwa”; broad Arabic usage permits this wording.
rows.anchor: جعلت المشورة فتيا. وذلك جائز لسعة العربية

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah reads qāḍiyatan in place of qāṭiʿatan; both mean that she would not decide an affair without them.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله (ما كنت قاضية أمرا) والمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen answers her advisers' claim of strength: if kings enter your lands, they humiliate you, even though you are rulers; God confirms this pattern.
rows.anchor: فقالت: إنهم إن دخلوا بلادكم أذلوكم وأنتم ملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif drops from mā when it means ayy shayʾ and joins a preposition, distinguishing an interrogative from a declarative; retaining it is also correct.
rows.anchor: نقصت الألف من قوله (بم) لأنها في معنى بأي شيء يرجع المرسلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal transmits an unnamed poet's line retaining the alif in fīmā, an example of the permitted full form.
rows.anchor: وأنشدنى المفضل: إنا قتلنا بقتلانا سراتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal also transmits an unnamed poet's line with ʿalā mā, likewise illustrating retention of the alif.
rows.anchor: على ما قام يشتمنا لئيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen's “to them” refers to Solomon.
rows.anchor: وهي تعني سليمان كقوله (على خوف من فرعون وملائهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the envoy was reportedly one woman, the queen uses the plural for him; the next verse's singular means “when the messenger came to Solomon.”
rows.anchor: رسولها- فيما ذكروا- امرأة واحدة فجمعت وإنما هو رسول

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah reads the plural “when they came to Solomon,” matching the earlier plural “messengers”; singular and plural are both valid for the single envoy.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله (فلما جاءوا سليمان) لما قال (المرسلون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon addresses the queen's messenger with a singular command; the command identifies the addressee as her envoy.
rows.anchor: يدل على ذلك قول سليمان (ارجع إليهم)

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah reads irjiʿū in the plural; using the singular for a group is common Arabic, as in 65:1.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله (ارجعوا إليهم) وهو صواب على ما فسرت لك

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah's codex reads lahum bihim instead of lahum bihā; the two expressions are equivalent.
rows.anchor: لا قبل لهم بها [37] وهي في مصحف عبد الله (لهم بهم) وهو سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abd Allah and Hamza read two nūns with yāʾ; Hamza assimilates them with a doubled nūn. ʿĀṣim reads two nūns without yāʾ; all forms are sound.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بنونين وباء مثبتة. وقرأها حمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ is absent from the written text in ā-tāni; readers who permit adding omitted yāʾs and wāws can restore it, but al-Farrāʾ prefers the consonantal text when Arab usage and the readers support it.
rows.anchor: اتباع المصحف إذا وجدت له وجها من كلام العرب وقراءة القراء أحب إلي من خلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ does not recommend Abu ʿAmr's additions, including a yāʾ in inna hādhayni and a wāw in fa-aṣṣaddaq; he will not venture the former reading.
rows.anchor: لساحران) ولست أجترئ على ذلك وقرأ (فأصدق وأكون)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIfrīt means strong and forceful; Arabs also say ʿifrīya. Its plural may be ʿafār for ʿifrīya, or ʿafārīt and sometimes ʿafār for ʿifrīt.
rows.anchor: القوي النافذ. ومن العرب من يقول للعفريت: عفرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keys of Qarun's treasuries weigh down a band of forty men; maftāḥ means a treasury, and their weight makes the men lean.
rows.anchor: نوؤها بالعصبة أن تثقلهم، والعصبة هاهنا أربعون رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the preposition, say tanūʾu bihim or tunīʾu bihim; dropping it adds an initial alif to the verb, as in atūnī afriġ and fa-aj āʾahā al-makhāḍ, understood with an omitted bi.
rows.anchor: قلت: تنوء بهم وتنيء بهم، كما قال (آتوني أفرغ عليه قطرا)

rows.speaker: رجل من أهل العربية
rows.claim: Another grammarian makes the band the subject weighed down by the keys, shifting the verb to mafātiḥ; al-Farrāʾ accepts it only if supported by transmitted usage, otherwise rejecting it as a misunderstanding.
rows.anchor: ما إن العصبة لتنوء بمفاتحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line says the lamp adorns the eye, citing taḥlā as evidence for the alternate construction.
rows.anchor: إن سراجا لكريم مفخره ... تحلى به العين إذا ما تجهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed Arab poem uses nāʾ for an archer leaning to one side under a bow's weight.
rows.anchor: ناء في شق الثمال كاهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā sāʾaka wa-nāʾaka means what troubles and burdens you; alif is suppressed by parallelism, as in hanāʾan wa-marāʾan and amraʾan.
rows.anchor: ما ساءك وناءك من ذلك، ومعناه ما ساءك وأناءك، إلا أنه ألقى الألف لأنه متبع لساءك، كما قالت العرب:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same suppression appears in akaltu ṭaʿāman fa-hannaʾanī wa-marraʾanī, whose unpaired form is amraʾanī.
rows.anchor: فهنأني ومرأني، ومعناه، إذا أفردت: وأمرأني، فحذفت منه الألف

rows.speaker: ذكروا
rows.claim: They report that Moses told Qarun not to exult because Qarun belonged to Moses' people, despite following another religion.
rows.anchor: ذكروا أن موسى الذي قال له ذلك لأنه من قومه وإن كان على غير دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural people can be represented by a single man, just as 3:173 says “the people told them”; there the informant was one man from Ashjaʿ.
rows.anchor: وجمعه هاهنا وهو واحد كقول الله (الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāriḥīn would also be correct: fāriḥ describes people who will rejoice, while fariḥ describes those rejoicing now, like ṭāmiʿ/ṭamiʿ and sālis/salis.
rows.anchor: ولو قيل: الفارحين كان صوابا، كأن الفارحين: الذين يفرحون فيما يستقبلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Banū Dubayr poet uses sālis; ʿaḍāris means cold and derives from ʿaḍras, “cold,” showing the paired forms sālis and salis.
rows.anchor: ممكورة غرثى الوشاح السالس ... تضحك عن ذي أشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun claims he received the wealth because he possessed merit and knowledge that made him deserving of it.
rows.anchor: على فضل عندي، أي كنت أهله ومستحقا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another construal takes ʿindī as “that is how I see it,” linking Qarun's wording to 39:49.
rows.anchor: ويقال: (أوتيته على علم) ثم قال (عندي) أي كذاك أرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is plural, not dual, because the two generic categories are not specifically designated; Arabic shifts such a comparison to the collective plural, and both forms are valid.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل: يستويان لأنها عام، وإذا كان الاثنان غير مصمود لهما

rows.speaker: إبراهيم أو مجاهد
rows.claim: The lesser punishment means afflictions that befall people in this world, before God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection; al-Farrāʾ is unsure whether the report is from Ibrahim or Mujahid.
rows.anchor: عن منصور عن إبراهيم أو عن مجاهد- شك الفراء- في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers have lamā with a doubled mīm; Abd Allah reads bimā, while al-Kisāʾī and Hamza also read lamā.
rows.anchor: القراء جميعا على (لما صبروا) بتشديد الميم ونصب اللام. وهي في قراءة عبد الله (بما صبروا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on lām, mā is genitive; with fatḥa and a doubled mīm, it has no syntactic slot and functions as a particle.
rows.anchor: وموضع (ما) خفض إذا كسرت اللام. وإذا فتحت وشددت فلا موضع لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs adopted men whose appearance or manners they admired, gave them a biological son's inheritance share, and attributed them by lineage to the adopter; God calls this a false claim.
rows.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية إذا أعجب أحدهم جلد الرجل وظرفه ضمه إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adopted sons must be attributed to their biological fathers.
rows.anchor: ثم أمرهم فقال: ادعوهم لآبائهم [5] أي انسبوهم إلى آبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When their fathers are unknown, attribute them to their patrons, for example as so-and-so son of ʿAbd Allāh or ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
rows.anchor: فانسبوهم إلى نسبة مواليكم الذين لا تعرفون آباءهم: فلان بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no blame for unintended mistakes; sin concerns deliberate acts, and the second mā is genitive by coordination with the mā in fīmā.
rows.anchor: فيما لم تقصدوا له من الخطأ، إنما الإثم فيما تعمدتم

rows.speaker: عبد الله أو أبي
rows.claim: Abd Allah or Ubayy's reading adds “and he is a father to them”; this applies to every prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله أو أبي (النبي أولى بالمؤمنين من أنفسهم وهو أب لهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers had been fraternized, and a pact-brother once inherited from his deceased brother ahead of blood relatives; the Prophet's priority over believers did not make him their heir, so a pact-brother could not inherit either.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجل إذا مات عن أخيه الذي آخاه ورثه دون عصبته وقرابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance belongs by kinship under the rule that relatives have priority over one another; “in God's book” means in the Preserved Tablet with God.
rows.anchor: وأنزل (وأولوا الأرحام بعضهم أولى ببعض) فى الميراث

words: كل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers put kull in the accusative because the verb acts on its resumptive pronoun; nominative is also good, since kull with negation behaves like an indefinite, meaning nothing escaped recording.
rows.anchor: القراء مجتمعون على نصب (كل) لما وقع من الفعل على راجع ذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third messenger had been sent before the first two and rejected; the narrative mentions him later, so “we reinforced with a third” refers back to him.
rows.anchor: بالثالث الذي قبلهما كقولك: فعززنا بال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strengthening came through what the first messenger, Shimon, had taught the pair.
rows.anchor: التعزيز يقول: شددنا أمرهما بما علمهما الأول شمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers had been sent to Antioch.
rows.anchor: أرسلوا إلى أنطاكية . وهي

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd Allah reads “with the third”; the definite noun follows because the messenger had already been mentioned among the messengers, like asking where the two dirhams are after mentioning them.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله (فعززنا بالثالث) لأنه قد ذكر فى المرسلين

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads ʿazzaznā lightly; al-Farrāʾ says it has the same sense as shaddadnā, “we strengthened.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم (فعززنا) خفيفة. وهو كقولك: شددنا وشددنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here rajm means killing; most Quranic uses of rajm likewise mean killing, as in the people of Shuʿayb's threat.
rows.anchor: يريد: لنقتلنكم. وعامة ما كان في القرآن من الرجم فهو قتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers have ṭāʾirakum with alif; Arab speakers also say ṭayrukum for “your omen is with you.”
rows.anchor: القراء مجتمعون على (طائركم) بالألف. والعرب تقول: طيركم معكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathānī means repeated: the Qur'an repeatedly mentions reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: أي مكررا يكرر فيه ذكر الثواب والعقاب

words: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Skin shivers with fear when a punishment verse is revealed, then softens when a mercy verse comes.
rows.anchor: تقشعر خوفا من آية العذاب إذا نزلت (ثم تلين) عند نزول آية رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said that guards drag the disbeliever shackled to the Fire and cast him in, leaving his face as the only protection; the question's answer is implicit.
rows.anchor: يقال: إن الكافر تنطلق به الخزنة إلى النار مغلولا، فيقذف به في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutashākisūn means disagreeing; the divided owner is a parable for a disbeliever who worships conflicting deities.
rows.anchor: مختلفون. هذا مثل ضربه الله للكافر والمؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man who belongs wholly to one master represents the monotheistic believer.
rows.anchor: هو المؤمن الموحد. وقد قرأ العوام (سلما) وسلم وسالم متقاربان في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salm is a verbal noun of salima, while sālim is an adjective; the paired forms have close senses, as illustrated by several Arabic forms of ribḥ and salām.
rows.anchor: مصدر لقولك: سلم له سلما والعرب تقول: ربح ربحا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have read sāliman.
rows.anchor: عن أبي روق عن إبراهيم التيمي عن ابن عباس أنه قرأ (ورجلا سالما)

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid is also reported to have read sāliman.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قرأ (سالما)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathalan is singular because the two men form one parable; likewise Mary and her son are called one sign, though the dual would also be valid.
rows.anchor: لأنهما جميعا ضربا مثلا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun is generic and has a plural sense; Abd Allah's plural reading confirms this interpretation.
rows.anchor: (الذي) غير موقت، فكأنه في مذهب جماع في المعنى

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب وأبو جعفر المدني
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab and Abu Jaʿfar al-Madanī read ʿibādihi, plural; other readers have ʿabdihi, singular.
rows.anchor: قرأها يحيى بن وثاب وأبو جعفر المدني (أليس الله بكاف عباده) على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh threatened that their gods would harm the Prophet for criticizing them; this prompted the reassurance that God suffices for His servant.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن قريشا قالت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawlā means walī, protector or ally; Abd Allah's reading has walī, as in 5:55, with the same sense.
rows.anchor: ذلك بأن الله ولي الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nār is nominative through al-mathwā; another valid parsing puts al-mathwā in the accusative and nominative al-nār is governed by the lām in lahum.
rows.anchor: ترفع النار بالمثوى، ولو نصبت المثوى، ورفعت النار باللام التي في (لهم) كان وجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the town whose people drove you to Medina; saying alladhī akhrajūka would also be grammatical, like a feminine town followed by masculine inhabitants.
rows.anchor: يريد: التي أخرجك أهلها إلى المدينة، ولو كان من قريتك التي أخرجوك كان وجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One tafsir makes this past: they had no helper when destroyed; another supplies kāna and means they now have no defender from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير: فلم يكن لهم ناصر حين أهلكناهم، فهذا وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is generic and means one person or many, so the text gives the plural their desires; similar singular-relative/plural-verb constructions occur in 21:82, 6:25, and 10:42.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن من تكون في معنى واحد وجميع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains mathal al-janna as the descriptions of Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: مثل الجنة، أمثال الجنة، صفات الجنة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib is reported to have read the plural amthāl.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قرأها علي بن أبي طالب: أمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āsin means changed or putrid; the water is neither changed nor stale.
rows.anchor: من ماء غير آسن (15) . غير متغير، غير آجن

words: أنهار من لبن لم يتغير طعمه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The milk of Paradise has not changed in taste and does not come from the udders of camels or sheep with their foam.
rows.anchor: لم يخرج من ضروع الإبل ولا الغنم برغوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ladhdhatan may be genitive as a description of the wine itself, adjective-like for the streams, or accusative as a verbal noun meaning it is enjoyed pleasurably.
rows.anchor: اللذة مخفوضة، وهي الخمر بعينها، وإن شئت جعلتها تابعة للأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular reading refers to Muhammad; those reading the plural include earlier prophets, whose peoples also threatened them, as in Shuʿayb's story. Both readings are sound.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله (أليس الله بكاف عبده) محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم، فكيف يخوفونك بمن دونه

rows.speaker: عاصم والحسن وشيبة المدني
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim, al-Ḥasan, and Shayba al-Madanī use nunation in both participles; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads them in construct form. Both are valid.
rows.anchor: نون فيهما عاصم والحسن وشيبة المدني. وأضاف يحيى بن وثاب. وكل صواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For an action already past in meaning, al-Farrāʾ favors construct form over nunation; a genuinely future action permits either form, while nunation is poor for a past action like “Hamza's killer.”
rows.anchor: فإذا رأيت الفعل قد مضى في المعنى فآثر الإضافة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says God takes the living in sleep when their appointed term ends; another says their being taken is sleep itself. Al-Farrāʾ prefers the latter.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إن توفيها نومها. وهو أحب الوجهين إلي لقوله (فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both qaḍā ʿalayhā al-mawt and quḍiya ʿalayhā al-mawt are read.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ (قضى عليها الموت) (وقضي عليها الموت) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun agrees with fitna; masculine huwa fitna is also valid, as the Qur'an elsewhere uses masculine hādhā with feminine raḥma.
rows.anchor: خرجت (هي) بالتأنيث لتأنيث الفتنة. ولو قيل: بل هو فتنة لكان صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in qālahā refers to an implied feminine word, such as kalima; masculine qālahu would also be correct.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله: (قد قالها الذين من قبلهم) أنثت إرادة الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine faʿlata in the reproach may instead be masculine faʿl, just as Arabic allows both feminine and masculine reference to an understood act.
rows.anchor: يجوز مكانها لو أتى: وفعلت فعلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istakh affa qawmahu means he incited and stirred up his people.
rows.anchor: وقوله: فاستخف قومه (54) يريد: استفزهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āsafūnā means they angered Us.
rows.anchor: وقوله: فلما آسفونا (55) يريد: أغضبونا

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads sulufan with a rounded vowel and doubled consonant; al-Qasim says he heard its singular sulaif, while the common reading is salaf.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش عن يحيى بن وثاب أنه قرأها: (سلفا) مضمومة مثقلة

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads salafan as a group of people, as though its singular were salfa, meaning a portion of people like an umma.
rows.anchor: حدثنا سفيان بن عيينة أن الأعرج قرأها: (فجعلناهم سلفا)

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh reports that ʿĀṣim left Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥmān's reading and used the alternate yaṣuddūn form.
rows.anchor: حدثني أبو بكر بن عياش عن عاصم: أنه ترك يصدون من قراءة أبي عبد الرحمن، وقرأ يصدون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have read yaṣiddūn, meaning they clamor and make noise.
rows.anchor: أن ابن عباس [171/ ب] قرأ: (يصدون) أي: يضجون يعجون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ replies that Arabs use both vowel patterns, like shadda/shidda and namma/nimma, and say ṣadda minhu or ʿanhu.
rows.anchor: العرب تقول: يصد ويصد مثل: يشد ويشد، وينم وينم من النميم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās challenged the reading to Ibn ʿUmayr's nephew, saying his cousin was an Arab and asking why he mispronounced the verse.
rows.anchor: إن ابن عمك لعربى فما له يلحن في قوله: (إذا قومك منه يصدون)

rows.speaker: أبي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading has dhikr for ʿilm; Ibn ʿAbbās is reported with ʿilm both with and without tanwin. All readings are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي: «وإنه لذكر للساعة» ، وقد روى عن ابن عباس: «وإنه لعلم للساعة»

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The Medinese read yā ʿibādī, retaining the yāʾ; the common reading omits it.
rows.anchor: «يا عبادي» . بإثبات الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kūb is a round-topped vessel without a handle.
rows.anchor: والكوب: المستدير الرأس الذي لا أذن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdī ibn Zayd's poem uses kūb for a cup served by a servant.
rows.anchor: متكئا تصفق أبوابه ... يسقي عليه العبد بالكوب

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The Medinan codices add a pronoun: tashtahīhi al-anfusu wa-taladhdhu, “the souls desire it and delight.”
rows.anchor: وفي مصاحف أهل المدينة: تشتهيه الأنفس وتلذ» .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They listen to the Prophet's Friday sermon without understanding; after leaving with the people they mockingly ask the Muslims what he just said, and God describes their sealed hearts.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يستمع إليك (16) . يعنى خطبتك فى الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mockery increases the guidance of those who have been guided.
rows.anchor: زادهم استهزاؤهم هدى، وآتاهم الله تقواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God rewarded them for their piety.
rows.anchor: يقال: أثابهم ثواب تقواهم، ويقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God inspired them with their piety.
rows.anchor: ويقال: ألهمهم تقواهم، ويقال: آتاهم تقواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says they received their piety from the abrogated rule when the abrogating verse came.
rows.anchor: ويقال: آتاهم تقواهم من المنسوخ إذا نزل الناسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers open an in an taʾtiyahum; Abu ʿAmr instead argues for conditional in taʾtihim, with the following clause as its result, a view al-Farrāʾ reports after consulting al-Ruʾāsī.
rows.anchor: (أن) مفتوحة فى القراءة كلها. حدثنا الفراء قال: وحدثني أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr says the construction is conditional in taʾtihim, with fa-qad jāʾa as the answer; some Kufan codices likewise omit the alif, though no reader used that form.
rows.anchor: إنما هي (إن تأتهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ also analyzes the phrase as a repetition of “Are they awaiting the Hour?”; in that parse an is accusative by apposition to al-sāʿa, while a jussive conditional restart is possible.
rows.anchor: وهو من المكرر: هل ينظرون إلا الساعة، هل ينظرون إلا أن تأتيهم بغتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual feminine subject is followed by a plural verb; Abd Allah's reading substitutes “make peace between them” and has an alternate sequence for when one side returns to God's command.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل: اقتتلتا، وهى فى قراءة عبد الله: فخذوا بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse followed a clash between Abdullah ibn Ubayy's and Abdullah ibn Rawaha's groups: after the Prophet's donkey defecated near Ibn Ubayy, he complained; Ibn Rawaha defended the Prophet, and both groups fought with hands and sandals.
rows.anchor: حتى اقتتلوا بالأيدي والنعال، فنزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual akhawaykum is used; ikhwat and ikhwān would also be correct forms for “your brothers.”
rows.anchor: ولم يقل: بين إخوتكم، ولا إخوانكم، ولو قيل ذلك كان صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressing side is the one that refuses reconciliation; the Prophet reconciled the disputants.
rows.anchor: التي لا تقبل الصلح، فأصلح النبي صلى الله عليه بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thabit ibn Qays, hard of hearing, crossed people to get near the Prophet's sermon; a man refused to make room, and Thabit later insulted the man's mother, hurting him and occasioning the verse.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أن ثابت بن قيس الأنصاري كان ثقيل السمع

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: In Abd Allah's reading the clause is plural ʿasaw an yakūnū khayran minhum; for women it is ʿasayna an yakunna khayran minhunna.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله فيما أعلم: عسوا أن يكونوا خيرا منهم

words: إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى وجعلناكم شعوبا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about human origins and peoples was also revealed in connection with the same incident.
rows.anchor: إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى وجعلناكم شعوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿūb are larger groupings than qabāʾil, which in turn are larger than afkhādh, clans or branches.
rows.anchor: والشعوب أكبر من القبائل، والقبائل أكبر من الأفخاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that people recognize one another by lineage.
rows.anchor: ليعرف بعضكم بعضا في النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna is read with kasra because the statement about the most honored is not governed by the purpose clause li-taʿārafū.
rows.anchor: (إن أكرمكم) مكسورة لم يقع عليها التعارف
